post.description:
Pre-check whether an ontology can answer a question, reporting coverage for
each of the four layers (ontology, terms, metrics, facts) and, for every
gap, what is missing and how to fix it.

Read-only. A layer whose inputs are not available reports status
`unavailable` (or `not_applicable`) and no coverage value; it is never
silently reported as zero coverage.

get.description:
Describe the namespace's queryable schema: classes and their properties
across every ontology loaded into the namespace (induced, foundational,
uploaded). Proxies to the ontology-engine ``/graph/schema`` route via the
ontology-api-proxy Lambda — the same source the MCP ``describe_schema``
tool reads, so an agent and a UI see the same schema.

post.description:
Runs one SPARQL SELECT or ASK in the SPARQL console.

The query is confined to the namespace's own graphs: they form the default
graph and each stays addressable as a named graph. The statement is refused
when it carries `FROM` / `FROM NAMED`, uses `SERVICE` or `LOAD`, names a graph
outside the namespace, is not SELECT/ASK, runs longer than 10 seconds, or
produces more than 4 MiB. At most 5,000 rows are returned; `truncated` says
whether the provider produced more.

AccessDeniedErrorResponseContent.description: Returned with HTTP 403 when the caller lacks permission to perform the requested operation.

message.description: Human-readable description of the authorization failure.

AnswerCandidate.description: A ranked candidate for the question as a whole.

ontologyVersion.description: Ontology version to check against; defaults to the published current one.

minCoverage.description: Minimum term coverage (0..1) required for `answerable: true`.

answerable.description:
True when the question can be answered: term coverage meets the
threshold, or an exact metric match supports a definition answer even
when no fact rows are available.

valueAnswerable.description: True when a concrete numeric value can be produced (facts layer covered).

answerMode.description: How the question can be answered: `value`, `definition` or `none`.

degraded.description: True when any layer is degraded or unavailable.

coverage.description: Character coverage of the ontology/term layer (0..1).

ontologyVersion.description: Ontology version the check ran against.

ontologyGraph.description: Named graph URI of that version.

termSource.description: Human-readable description of the term source used.

layers.description: Exactly four layers, in order: ontology, terms, metrics, facts.

missing.description: One entry per gap, each carrying what is missing and how to fix it (F79).

candidates.description: Ranked candidates that could close the gaps.

hint.description: Operator-facing next step when `answerable` is false.

ConfidenceScore.description:
A confidence score in [0, 1] for a query result, with an optional rationale
explaining how it was derived.

rationale.description: Explanation of how the score was derived.

ConformanceWarning.description:
A warning raised when a result row does not conform to the expected SHACL
shape, identifying the offending row and shape.

row.description: Index of the result row that failed conformance.

shape.description: Identifier of the SHACL shape that was violated.

message.description: Human-readable description of the conformance warning.

CoverageChars.description: Character accounting behind the ontology/term coverage ratio.

covered.description: Number of content characters covered by a matched term.

total.description: Number of content characters in the question (stopwords/punctuation removed).

CoverageLayer.description: One of the four answerability layers.

coverage.description:
Layer coverage in 0..1. Absent when the layer cannot be computed;
clients must render that as "unavailable", never as 0.

matched.description:
Evidence that matched in this layer. Fields are layer-specific: ontology
and term matches carry id/label/predicate/source, metrics carry
id/label/score, facts carry metricId/status/code/observationRows.

missing.description: Short human-readable descriptions of what this layer lacks.

DataSourceUnavailableErrorResponseConten.description:
Returned with HTTP 502 when a backing data source cannot be reached to
answer the query; `dataSourceId` identifies the unavailable source.

dataSourceId.description: Identifier of the data source that could not be reached.

classes.description: The classes in the namespace's schema.

DimensionFilter.description:
A filter constraining a query to rows matching a dimension value, with an
optional comparison operator (defaults to equality).

Server-side invariants NOT expressible as Smithy traits, enforced at
validation (a violation is a 400, see the Context Manager's InvokeRequest):
  - `name` must be non-blank, and is trimmed before use.
  - `name` is matched case-insensitively, and must be UNIQUE across the list —
    a mapping cannot express two values for one dimension. (`@uniqueItems`
    would not capture this: it compares whole structures, so two filters on
    the same name with different values would still pass.)
  - every filter must be applicable by the resolved metric; a filter the
    metric cannot apply fails closed rather than being dropped.

name.description: Name of the dimension to filter on.

value.description:
Value to match for the dimension. For compatibility, the server also
accepts a JSON number (finite) or boolean here and binds it as a typed
literal; `null`, objects, and arrays are rejected.

DimensionOperator.description:
Comparison operator applied by a DimensionFilter.

Equality is the only supported comparison: Tier-1 binds the value as a bare
SQL literal into a governed metric's template, which expresses `=` and nothing
else. Declared as an enum rather than a free-form String so a client asking
for an unsupported comparison is rejected by the contract instead of having it
silently applied as equality — a wrong answer returned with a 200.

Entity.description:
An entity (graph node) with its IRI, human-readable label, optional type, and
arbitrary properties.

type.description: Type (class IRI) of the entity, if known.

GapCandidate.description: A ranked candidate that may close a gap.

GraphContext.description:
Graph context accompanying an answer: the entities and relationships that
were traversed or cited.

entities.description:
Entities traversed or cited for the answer. Bounded to 200 entities per
response; a traversal that reached more is reported through
`metadata.degradedSources` and the processing trace.

relationships.description:
Relationships traversed or cited for the answer. Bounded to 500
relationships per response; a traversal that reached more is reported
through `metadata.degradedSources` and the processing trace. A relationship
the graph carries without a predicate identifier cannot be represented (see
`predicateUri`) and is reported the same way, so an empty list is never
ambiguous between "none found" and "all discarded".

startUri.description: IRI of the entity to start traversal from.

maxDepth.description:
Maximum traversal depth from the starting entity. Defaults to 2.
Depths above 2 are accepted but currently traverse 2 hops.

relationshipFilter.description:
Accepted and validated, but not yet applied: traversal currently
follows every relationship. Reserved for restricting traversal to
these relationship (predicate) IRIs.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of entities to return. Defaults to 100.

InternalServerErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 500 when the service fails unexpectedly. The message is a
fixed, generic description; the underlying cause is logged, never returned.

message.description: Generic description of the failure; carries no internal detail.

topK.description: Maximum number of chunks to return.

minScore.description:
Minimum relevance score a chunk must meet to be returned. Relevance
scores are non-negative; no upper bound is set because the scale
depends on the index's similarity metric.

sourceFilter.description:
Not yet supported; a non-empty value is rejected with 400. Reserved
for restricting results to these source document identifiers. An
empty list is accepted and restricts nothing.

entityFilter.description:
Not yet supported; a non-empty value is rejected with 400. Reserved
for restricting results to chunks annotated with these entities. An
empty list is accepted and restricts nothing.

chunks.description: Ranked supporting chunks matching the query.

queryEmbeddingModel.description: Identifier of the embedding model used for the query.

id.description: Matched identifier (term IRI or metric id).

predicate.description: Predicate that produced the match (ontology layer).

metricId.description: Metric this evidence belongs to (facts layer).

status.description: Fact coverage status for that metric.

observationRows.description: Number of fact rows backing the metric.

factFunction.description: Fact function declared by the metric.

MatchedTerm.description: A term that matched part of the question.

span.description: Inclusive-exclusive [start, end) character span in the normalized question.

MissingGap.description: A gap: what is missing, in which layer, and how to fix it (F79).

text.description: The question fragment that could not be covered (ontology layer).

span.description: Inclusive-exclusive [start, end) span of that fragment, when known.

what.description: What exactly is missing, phrased as an operator action target.

metricId.description: Metric this gap belongs to (facts layer).

nearbyTerms.description: Lexically nearby terms that may be the intended concept.

candidates.description: Ranked candidates that may close this gap.

NamespaceNotFoundErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 404 when the target namespace does not exist or is not
visible to the caller.

namespaceId.description: Identifier of the namespace that was not found.

NearbyTerm.description: A lexically similar term offered for an uncovered fragment.

NoResultErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 404 when a pinned tier produced no data for the query —
a "no results" outcome rather than a server error.

tier.description: Pinned tier that produced no result (1 = metric match, 2 = structured query).

OntologyNotPublishedErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 409 when the namespace has no published ontology, so the
query cannot be resolved against a schema yet.

namespaceId.description: Identifier of the namespace whose ontology is not published.

PropertyMap.description:
String-valued entity properties. `supportingStatements` is reserved for a
JSON-encoded string array of graph-only evidence. It is bounded to 100
statements per entity, 1,000 characters and 2,000 UTF-8 bytes per statement,
and 4,000 characters and 6,000 UTF-8 bytes across an assembled graph context.

QueryMode.description: Tier-3 execution mode for a query. Orthogonal to the tier cascade.

execute.description: Whether to execute the generated query (versus translate only).

tierOverride.description: Pin resolution to a specific tier (1, 2 or 3), bypassing automatic routing.

dimensions.description: Dimension filters to constrain the query.

timeoutMs.description:
Maximum time to wait for the query, in milliseconds. A caller may
narrow the service's own REST budget (29,000 ms) but not widen it.

includeSupporting.description:
Whether to include supporting content in the response. When false,
`supportingContent` and the `supportingStatements` property of each
`graphContext` entity are omitted; the entities and relationships are
still returned.

includeDebugInfo.description:
When true, include the generated SQL (`queryUsed`) and SPARQL
(`sparqlGenerated`) in the response for debugging and observability.
Defaults to false; when unset or false, both fields are omitted.

**Security:** these fields expose internal schema (table and column
names, joins), so the flag is honoured only for a caller who already
administers that schema: a platform admin, or a namespace owner,
maintainer or data steward of the queried namespace. For any other
caller the request still succeeds, but both fields are omitted as if
the flag were false.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of result rows to return.

requestId.description: Identifier of the request, for tracing and support.

sessionId.description: Identifier of the session the request belongs to.

QueryResult.description:
The top-level result of a query: the answering tier, confidence, tabular
rows and/or a synthesized answer, the query that ran, supporting content,
graph context, and an execution trace.

tier.description: The answering tier that produced this result.

resultRows.description: Tabular result rows returned by the query.

synthesizedAnswer.description: Natural-language answer synthesized from the results.

queryUsed.description: The query that was executed to produce the result.

sparqlGenerated.description: The SPARQL query generated for the result, if any.

trace.description: Step-by-step execution trace of the query.

ontologyVersion.description: Version of the ontology the query ran against.

dataSources.description: Identifiers of the data sources that contributed to the result.

executionMode.description:
The execution mode that produced this result: "standard" or
"deep-reasoning". Deep Reasoning is a mode orthogonal to the tier
cascade, so a client labels an answer by this field rather than
inferring mode from `tier` (a Deep Reasoning answer resolves at tier 3
but is not Standard mode's Tier-3 result). Absent on responses that do
not set it.

QueryStrategy.description:
Which Tier-2 engine answers a structured query. Absent = the serve default
(``nl_to_sql_first``).

This is a DIFFERENT axis from ``mode``: ``mode`` chooses whether the whole
T1→T2→T3 cascade is replaced by the Tier-3 reasoning loop, while ``strategy``
chooses which engine answers within Tier 2. Both were called "agentic" before
the rebrand, which is why the distinction is spelled out here.

An explicit value is caller intent and is never overridden by automatic tier
gating or per-query Tier-2 pruning.

QueryTranslationErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 400 when a natural-language question cannot be translated
into an executable query against the ontology.

RateLimitExceededErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 429 when the caller exceeds the request rate limit;
`retryAfterSeconds` indicates how long to wait before retrying.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Number of seconds to wait before retrying the request.

Relationship.description:
A directed relationship between two entities, identified by source, predicate,
and target IRIs.

predicateUri.description:
IRI of the predicate linking source to target. A property-graph edge that
carries only a human-readable predicate string is given a stable,
tenant-scoped synthetic identifier in the `urn:coa:graph-predicate:` scheme,
derived from that string. Treat such a value as an opaque identity for
correlating edges within one namespace, not as an ontology predicate IRI.

additionalProperties.description:
Customer data returned by or sent to a query: result cell values, knowledge-base
chunk text, synthesized answers, generated SQL/SPARQL, and dimension filter
values. Marked sensitive so generated clients keep it out of logs.

RunSparqlRequestContent.description: The namespace and the statement to run.

sparql.description: SPARQL text: one SELECT or ASK statement.

RunSparqlResponseContent.description: One executed statement: its form, the ASK answer, or the SELECT columns and rows.

answer.description: The ASK answer; present only when `form` is `ASK`.

items.description: One variable name, without the leading `?`.

variables.description: Column names, in the provider's order (SELECT only).

items.description:
One RDF term: an IRI as-is, a literal with its language/datatype suffix,
or a blank node as `_:id`.

rowCount.description: Rows the provider produced before the 5,000-row display cap (SELECT only).

returnedRows.description: Rows actually returned in `rows` (SELECT only; at most 5,000).

truncated.description: True when the provider produced more than 5,000 rows and `rows` was cut.

graphCount.description: Number of namespace graphs the query was confined to.

SchemaClass.description:
A class in the namespace's queryable schema, with its IRI, label, optional
description, properties, and parent class.

parentClass.description: IRI of the parent class, if any.

SchemaProperty.description:
A property of a schema class, with its IRI, label, value range (datatype or
target class), and optional description.

range.description: Value range of the property (datatype or target class).

ServiceUnavailableErrorResponseContent.description:
Returned with HTTP 503 when the service, or a required dependency (including
one it needs to handle the request safely), is temporarily unavailable. For
example, a create that
carries a `clientToken` fails closed with this error when the retry-safety
store cannot be reached, rather than risk running the create twice. Retry
the request (with the same `clientToken`) after a backoff.

message.description:
Description of the unavailable dependency or operation; carries no
internal detail.

SparqlProviderErrorResponseContent.description: The provider could not execute the statement.

message.description: Human-readable description of the provider failure.

providerMessage.description: The provider's own message, truncated for display.

SparqlResultTooLargeErrorResponseContent.description: The result exceeded the 4 MiB response cap.

message.description: Human-readable description of the size refusal.

SparqlTimeoutErrorResponseContent.description: The statement exceeded the 10 second limit.

SupportingContent.description:
A knowledge-base chunk that supports an answer, with its text, source
document provenance, and relevance score.

sourceDocumentId.description:
Opaque, unique identifier of the source document the chunk came from.
Use this value to correlate chunks; it is not a display name.

sourceDocumentName.description:
Human-readable original file name of the source document. This value is
intended for display and is not guaranteed to be unique.

relevanceScore.description: Relevance score of the chunk to the query.

TraceStep.description:
One step in a query's execution trace, recording what ran, its status,
timing, and any tool used or conformance warnings raised.

status.description: Status of the step (e.g. success or failure).

durationMs.description: Duration of the step in milliseconds.

toolUsed.description: Name of the tool invoked during the step, if any.

parallelGroup.description: Identifier of the parallel group this step ran in, if any.

wallMs.description: Wall-clock time for the step in milliseconds.

conformanceWarnings.description: Conformance warnings raised during the step.

query.description: Natural-language question to translate into SPARQL.

sparqlQuery.description: The SPARQL query generated from the question.

ontologyVersion.description: Version of the ontology the query was generated against.

TraversalDirection.description: Direction to follow relationships when traversing the graph.

message.description: Human-readable description of the validation failure.
